title: 3A-VLA: Abstraction-Aligned Action Learning for Vision-Language Agents in 3D Game Worlds
claim: Prior models map inputs directly to actions; ours aligns action learning with intention and environment abstractions to ground decisions semantically.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, left-to-right, red align/reweight links under ours
description: A dashed vertical line splits the figure into (a) Previous VLA on the left and (b) Our 3A-VLA on the right. In (a), gray Text Tokenizer and Image Tokenizer boxes feed into a single VLA box, then an Action De-Tokenizer, giving the output 'Action'. Next to it is a PvP game screenshot with a thought bubble reading 'Defeat the nearby enemy', and the output 'aim → shoot'. In (b), the same tokenizers feed a light-blue 3A-VLA block. That block branches into three colored detokenizers: green Action, orange Intention and darker orange Environ. Red arrows and labels ('reweight', 'align') link the Action output, IA and ESA. At the right is a screenshot overlaid with a labeled semantic grid (Wall, Sky, Enemy, Player, Road, Other). It has red boxes around 'wall' and an intention sentence, and ends in 'move left → aim → shoot'.
caption: Unlike previous VLA models which mapped low-level inputs directly to actions, 3A-VLA aligns action learning with intention abstraction (IA) and environment semantics abstraction (ESA) through multimodal detokenizers. As shown in a PvP scenario, 3A-VLA grounds instructions and visual scenes into high-level, interpretable concepts such as "wall" and "enemy". (i) When trained on action sequences such as "move left, aim, shoot," the model learns the semantic relationship between "wall" and "move left," recognizing the object's functional role as tactical cover rather than merely its presence. (ii) When tasked with locating off-screen enemies, the model uses the structured affordance representation from the ESA to reason about likely ambush points, such as inferring that a "wall" may serve as high-probability cover from which an opponent could emerge, thereby enabling proactive searches. In off-screen scenarios with weak IA-ESA correlation, semantic reasoning outweighs action prediction; 3A-VLA adapts by reweighting action learning to prioritize semantic grounding.
abstract: Despite advances in vision-language-action (VLA) models, they remain limited in highly dynamic game settings such as 3D open worlds and competitive player versus player (PvP) settings, where agents must efficiently extract sparse, actionable signals from dense visual input while integrating multimodal cues to track off-screen high-value targets in real time. To address this, we introduce 3A-VLA (Abstraction-Aligned Action VLA), a framework that grounds action learning in explicit intention and environment abstractions rather than superficial pattern matching. We introduce dual task-agnostic abstractions: the intention abstraction (IA), which condenses verbose instructions and reasoning into explicit semantic primitives, and the environment semantics abstraction (ESA), which structures dense visual streams into a spatial-functional affordance representation to guide grounded actions. We further propose an abstraction alignment reweighting (AAR) module that adaptively reweights the action imitation loss. A continuous intention-environment alignment signal is used to emphasize reliable action supervision when abstractions agree and reduce the influence of ambiguous demonstrations when they diverge, thereby learning a policy that balances fine-grained control and high-level reasoning without the need for manual rules. Extensive experiments show that 3A-VLA performs competitively among the evaluated baselines in both open-world (Minecraft) and competitive PvP (Game for Peace) settings. It also demonstrates zero-shot combat transfer from Game for Peace to high-fidelity games, including Valorant, CS2, GTA V, Elden Ring, and Mount & Blade.
